source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check end-of-POST status is normal.
1. Check the information of test item

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Information should be correct and still be correct after rebooting

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ls /sys/class/mei/ 2>&1; echo ---; mei-amt-check -P 2>&1 || echo "End-of-POST Status tool not installed"; echo ---; dmesg | grep -iE "post" | tail -20
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: read the end-of-POST status (End-of-POST Status) via the MEI/SPS channel. The agent collects whatever MEI/SPS registers/dmesg lines are reachable; confirming the value is CORRECT requires knowing the expected value (a user-supplied baseline), so this is PARTIAL: agent returns the raw readout, user judges it against the expected End-of-POST Status.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: read-only attempt against Intel MEI/SPS registers using vendor tools (intelmetool / mei-amt-check) that may not be installed on the SUT; install/availability must be confirmed first, and the expected baseline value must be provided by the user.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; recognizes a status read but does not establish -P field semantics/read-only behavior, authoritative source or post-reboot evidence.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; requires expected POST state, platform decoder, read-only BIOS/ME/BMC source and reboot recovery evidence.
historical_reviews.round_02: PARTIAL; uses generic dmesg text that cannot prove POST completion.
historical_reviews.second_review_handoff: Confirms an authoritative platform status source is needed and generic post text is insufficient.

original_test_intent: Read the platform's authoritative end-of-POST completion/status field, compare it with the owner-defined normal code/state and verify a normal completed POST is reported again after an approved reboot.
original_method: Use a validated read-only BIOS/ME/BMC POST-status source and decoder to capture raw completion state, perform one approved reboot while retaining boot/SEL evidence, then repeat the same query after the system reaches the defined post-boot stabilization point.
manual_activity: The owner supplies the authoritative field/normal state, validates the query and approves reboot/recovery; the engineer later issues the verdict. Query, reboot, boot monitoring, reconnect, repeat query and evidence capture can be automated when an electronic platform status source exists.
required_inputs: Exact platform/SKU and BIOS/ME/BMC firmware identities
Authoritative End-of-POST status source, raw code/state, decoder and sampling time
Expected boot milestones, timeout and post-boot stabilization condition
Maintenance approval, active-workload check, KVM/OOB recovery and evidence path
safety_requirements: Do not change BIOS/ME/BMC settings or remediate POST within this read-only case.
Do not infer POST completion from generic kernel dmesg 'post' text.
Preserve prior POST/SEL/boot evidence and obtain approval before reboot.
Stop on ambiguous status identity, POST timeout, boot loop, new fault or reconnect failure; never auto-retry the reboot.
agent_execution_scope: Validate status field/decoder/query and capture platform identity, raw status and boot/BMC/SEL baseline.
Perform one approved reboot, monitor power/POST/boot milestones and reconnect within the defined timeout.
Repeat the status query after stabilization, compare expected/pre/post values and collect full boot/SEL evidence without remediation or a formal verdict.
engineer_actions: Define the authoritative End-of-POST state and approve the query/decoder.
Approve reboot, timeout and OOB/KVM recovery plan.
Review status and boot evidence and issue PASS/FAIL.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: MEI presence is ancillary, mei-amt-check -P semantics/read-only applicability are unverified and a generic dmesg grep does not prove firmware POST completion. The sequence omits reboot monitoring and the second read.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the platform-approved electronic BIOS/ME/BMC End-of-POST status query and decoder, with the identical query before and after one controlled reboot.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: End-of-POST normality, correctness after reboot and 5/0-minute fields are preserved; no status code is fabricated.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind a documented POST-completion field/code to BIOS/ME/BMC identities, collect structured pre/post status plus boot milestone timestamps, SEL and optional console capture around one approved reboot.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the platform/firmware combination that documents the chosen End-of-POST source.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS/ME/BMC, query/API, OS and kernel versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Use the platform vendor's POST status/boot progress and management-interface documentation supplied for execution.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines status semantics, boot timing and the omitted reboot/re-query chain.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; both state correctness and repeatability after reboot are retained.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Status source, decoder, expected code and boot timeout.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A host reaching OS does not necessarily prove the requested firmware status field; conversely a stale status must be distinguished by timestamps/boot identifiers.

project_override_considerations: A project defines the authoritative POST telemetry, expected code and timeout. These are readiness inputs, not automation limitations; results apply only to the identified firmware build and boot plan.
expected_evidence: Platform/SKU, BIOS/ME/BMC identity, POST status source/decoder and expected state
Raw pre-reboot status and preserved boot/SEL baseline
Approved reboot/power/POST/boot/reconnect timeline and raw post-stabilization status
Expected/pre/post comparison, boot/kernel/BMC/SEL health, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The request for normal End-of-POST status and post-reboot correctness is consistent. Missing field/decoder details are readiness gaps.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The POST-completion persistence intent is clear. Missing vendor telemetry/expected code delays execution but is not a permanent semantic blocker, and the core sequence is automatable.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains the read-only intent but rejects generic evidence and PARTIAL classification.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains authoritative-source, decoder and reboot controls while reclassifying to FULLY AUTOMATABLE because electronic POST telemetry removes any inherent manual core step.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Adds boot-instance timing/staleness controls and separates POST field status from generic OS boot success.

review_improvement: Prevents false POST claims from kernel text, ensures the result belongs to the tested boot and correctly distinguishes readiness/verdict from full electronic automation.
independent_technical_reasoning: A documented firmware/management POST status can be queried electronically and one reboot can be orchestrated and monitored. Owner-defined status and engineer judgment do not make the core partial, so FULLY AUTOMATABLE is correct.
